preamble: Depalatalization of the palatalized trill /rʲ/ to plain /r/ is documented in East Slavic. In Ukrainian and Belarusian, Common Slavic *rʲ was dispalatalized in the 10th–13th centuries, so that word-final soft r became hard, as in цар 'tsar' against Russian царь.
phoneticEffects: Depalatalization, Merger, Loss of Secondary Articulation

examples.from: Old East Slavic цьсарь (cĭsarĭ), final soft r
examples.note: Final *rʲ hardened in Ukrainian, while Russian keeps царь with soft r; the Carpathian (Hutsul) dialects did not take part in this dispalatalization.

examples.from: Old East Slavic цьсарь (cĭsarĭ), final soft r
examples.note: Belarusian has no palatalized r at all; every inherited *rʲ became plain /r/.

sources: Lebedivna, O. (2022). Dispalatalization of Common Slavic *ri̯ in Ukrainian: The case of family names in -uk- in the Hutsul parish registers. Ukrainska mova 2022(2), 110–122. https://doi.org/10.15407/ukrmova2022.02.110
